title: Living, Dead and Never Alive
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Living, Dead and Never Alive Worksheets (Sorting Things)
standard_code: Year 2: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on things that are living, dead and never alive: what living things do and sorting everyday things into groups. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Living things feed, grow and have young. Dead things were once alive.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things feed, grow and have young.

  • Dead things were once alive, like a dead leaf or paper.
  • Never alive things were never part of a living thing, like a rock.
  • Something that moves is not always alive.
Example

A wooden table?

Made from a tree

Answer: dead (was once alive)

Example

A metal spoon?

Not from a living thing

Answer: never alive

Common mistakes

  • Thinking things that move are alive, like a car.
  • Thinking plants are not alive.
  • Thinking a wooden table was never alive.

faq.q: How do we know something is alive?
faq.a: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. A plant is alive even though it does not walk.

faq.q: What is the difference between dead and never alive?
faq.a: Dead things were once alive, like a dead leaf, a feather or a wooden table. Never alive things, like a rock or a plastic bottle, were never part of a living thing.

faq.q: Is a car alive because it moves?
faq.a: No. A car cannot feed, grow or have young, so it is not alive.
